Mallat, *Multiresolution approximations and wavelet orthonormal bases of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 315 (1989), Section 4, after (70): the Haar basis is the wavelet orthonormal basis of the multiresolution approximation with scaling function $\mathbf{1}_{[0,1]}$).…

nodes.summary: The constant function $1$ together with the Haar functions $x \mapsto 2^{k/2} H(2^k x - j)$, $k \ge 0$, $0 \le j < 2^k$, supported in $[0,1)$ (DeVore's $H_{j,k}$), form an orthonormal basis of $L^2[0,1)$ (R. A. DeVore, *Nonlinear approximation*, Acta Numerica 7 (1998), Section 3.5, (3.44)–(3.47)). The Lean statement asserts a Hilbert basis of $L^2([0,1))$ indexed by…

It is the wavelet of the multiresolution approximation whose scaling function is $\mathbf{1}_{[0,1)}$:…
nodes.title: Haar function

nodes.summary: For $j, k \in \mathbb{Z}$, the Haar functions are supported on the dyadic interval $2^{-j}[k, k+1)$ and normalized in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ (S. Mallat, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 315 (1989), the family $\sqrt{2^j}\,\psi(2^j x - k)$ of Section 4 (after (70)) with $\psi = H$; R. A. DeVore, *Nonlinear approximation*, Acta Numerica 7 (1998), (3.41), for $j \ge 0$ and $0 \le k < 2^j$, where his indices are written $H_{k,j}$).
nodes.title: Haar system

nodes.summary: $\int_{\mathbb{R}} H(x)^2\,dx = 1$, since $H^2 = \mathbf{1}_{[0,1)}$. By the change of variables $y = 2^j x - k$, every Haar function $H_{j,k}$ then has unit norm in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$.
nodes.title: The Haar function has unit $L^2$ norm

nodes.summary: $\int_{\mathbb{R}} H(x)\,dx = \tfrac12 - \tfrac12 = 0$: the Haar wavelet has one vanishing moment, like the wavelets of other multiresolution bases (its Fourier transform vanishes at $0$). It has no second vanishing moment, $\int x H(x)\,dx = -1/4$, which is why Haar coefficients of smooth functions decay slowly.
nodes.title: The Haar function has mean zero

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
